correctness.rationale: For real circular BV with unnormalized L1, a displacement z of shortest length h satisfies the translation bound by integrating |Df| over oriented arcs of length h. A semicircle has variation 2, translated symmetric-difference length 2h, and pointwise differences of one sign at each x across all shifts, proving the probability-convolution norm without symmetry. Positive shift density forces equality in the translation bound for almost every h; opposite Jordan supports at distance < π would put positive masses of both on an open family of subsemicircular arcs, forcing strict cancellation. Cross-support distances must all be π, hence both Jordan parts are opposite atoms. The wrapped variance-2t Gaussian gives the triangular-distance Fourier series with the stated normalization; its derivative in phase is the positive Dirichlet heat evolution of 1 on (0,π). After multiplication by π exp(t)/4 the time derivative for β=|b|>0 is cos(βt)+βsin(βt) plus an O_β(exp(-8t)) C¹ remainder. Fixed disjoint neighborhoods of the leading zeros have derivative of fixed sign bounded away from zero, and the leading value is bounded away from zero outside them. This gives exactly one late zero per neighborhood, no other late zeros, the stated time error, and the signed value error after using cos(π/2+arctan β+nπ)=(-1)^(n+1)β/sqrt(1+β²). For b=0 every term of the derivative is positive. Replay: RESULT.md lines 33–58.
